passage:
Nazia, come here. Your Nani Ishita has something to tell you before your board exams.
In my Class 12, my whole hostel room crammed all night. I kept three things: bed at a fixed hour, a walk to the mango tree after dinner, and a proper meal. My friends laughed at me, and I felt silly for a day, but I kept my three. On the morning of the physics paper, half of them stared at the questions with blank faces. I remembered the derivation as if it were written on the wall.
I am not saying study less. I am saying the hour you save by not sleeping is often the hour you lose in the exam hall. Take your walk, beta.

qa.q: What three things did Ishita keep during exam season?
qa.a: A fixed bedtime, a walk to the mango tree after dinner, and a proper meal.

qa.q: How did Ishita feel when friends laughed, and what did Ishita do?
qa.a: Ishita felt a little silly for a day but kept the three habits anyway.

qa.q: What choice did young Ishita make that paid off on the day of the physics paper?
qa.a: Ishita kept sleep, a walk and a meal on schedule while others crammed all night, and remembered the derivation clearly.

qa.q: How might Ishita's friends have felt on the morning of the physics paper?
qa.a: Probably anxious and foggy, since half of them stared at the questions with blank faces after cramming all night.

grounding: An elder recalls keeping sleep, a walk and a meal during exams and remembering better than friends who crammed.

The chemistry paper was at nine the next morning, the corridor throbbed with someone's speaker, and Jasleen was waving a highlighter. "Sleep is a luxury tonight," she said. "We study till dawn."
Indu closed her notes at half past nine. She had already eaten a proper dinner and walked once round the hostel garden, listening to frogs. "If I can't answer it now, two more hours won't fix it," she said, and set her alarm.
Jasleen scoffed, but by midnight she was rereading the same page. In the hall Indu's mind was clear; she recalled the reaction steps in order and even had time to check. Jasleen yawned through the last question.

qa.q: When was the chemistry paper?
qa.a: At nine the next morning.

qa.q: What does Indu feel about closing her notes while Jasleen keeps studying?
qa.a: Indu seems calm and confident. She says two more hours won't fix what she cannot answer now, and she sets her alarm.

qa.q: What choice did Indu make that helped in the exam hall?
qa.a: She ate a proper dinner, took a walk and stopped studying at half past nine, so her mind was clear and she recalled the steps in order.

qa.q: How might Jasleen feel as midnight passes and she rereads the same page?
qa.a: Probably anxious and tired, since she is stuck on the same page and yawns through the last question.

grounding: A student in exam season keeps sleep, a walk and a meal on schedule despite noise and time pressure.

passage:
In the week before the board exams, the lights in Pradeep's flat across the lane in Indore stayed on till three every night. Raghav could see them from his balcony.
Raghav had a different schedule taped to his cupboard: study blocks till nine, dinner with the family, a twenty-minute walk round the colony, lights off by eleven. His mother had grumbled at first. "Only till nine? Pradeep studies all night!"
On the morning of the maths paper, Raghav walked to the bus stop feeling slow but clear. Pradeep was there already, eyes red. "I did the whole of integration last night," he said. "Now I can't remember the first formula."
Raghav handed him a biscuit. In the exam hall the formulas came back to Raghav one by one, like people walking into a room.

qa.q: By what time were Raghav's lights off?
qa.a: By eleven.

qa.q: How was Raghav feeling on the morning of the maths paper?
qa.a: Raghav felt slow but calm and clear-headed after keeping the schedule all week.

qa.q: Which parts of Raghav's routine protected his recall?
qa.a: Sleep by eleven, dinner with the family and a twenty-minute walk kept him rested, so the formulas came back in the hall.

qa.q: What was the morning like for Pradeep?
qa.a: Pradeep was exhausted and anxious, eyes red, unable to remember the first formula after studying all night.

grounding: Shows a student in exam season keeping sleep, a walk and meals on schedule, and recalling better than a friend who crammed all night.

passage:
"Samir, dinner. Now."
"Can't. Physics. I haven't done optics."
"You've been at that desk since lunch." Tenzin tapped the book. "Remember last term? You skipped dinner, stayed up till four and blanked in the paper."
"That was different."
"Was it? Come on. Dal, rice, one round of the football field. Forty minutes. Then optics."
Samir groaned. "If I fail, it's your fault."
"If you fail, it's the optics' fault."
They ate. They walked. On the field Samir said, "The lens formula, one over f equals..." and got it right without looking.
Back in the hostel room Samir did optics till ten, then shut the book. "Okay. Sleep. You win."

qa.q: What did Tenzin suggest before optics?
qa.a: Dal, rice and one round of the football field: forty minutes.

qa.q: Why did Samir resist going to dinner?
qa.a: Samir was anxious about not having done optics and felt every minute away from the desk was lost.

qa.q: What made Tenzin's approach persuasive?
qa.a: Tenzin reminded Samir of last term's blank and offered a short, specific plan with optics straight after.

qa.q: What would change if Samir had stayed up till four again?
qa.a: Samir might have blanked in the paper again, just as happened last term.

grounding: Shows a student in exam season choosing a meal, a walk and sleep over panicked extra hours, and recalling better for it.

passage:
Last March, during my Class 10 exams, I did something my friends thought was crazy. Every evening at seven I shut my books and went for a walk with my brother Yash around the lake near our house. We didn't talk about exams. We counted ducks, argued about cricket, bought roasted corn. At nine I ate dinner with everyone, and at ten-thirty I was asleep.
My friends were studying till two. On the phone they sounded shaky and snappish. Sometimes I felt guilty, as if I wasn't trying hard enough.
But in the science paper, when a question on circuits came up that I'd revised only once, the answer was just there. I think my brain had done the filing while I slept. I'm Usha, and I still walk to that lake before anything important.

qa.q: Where did Usha and Yash walk each evening?
qa.a: Around the lake near their house.

qa.q: How did Usha sometimes feel about the evening routine?
qa.a: Usha sometimes felt guilty, as if not trying hard enough, while friends studied till two.

qa.q: Why did Usha's routine help in the science paper?
qa.a: Regular sleep, walks and meals kept Usha rested, so an answer revised only once came back easily.

qa.q: What might the evening walks have meant for Yash?
qa.a: For Yash they were probably a relaxed time with a sibling, counting ducks and arguing about cricket, away from exam talk.

grounding: Shows a student keeping sleep, a walk and meals on schedule during exams, and recalling well in the paper.

passage:
Class teacher's note, board exam week
I've been watching two students this week. Bidisha has been studying till three every night; today she came in pale, forgot a formula she knew well, and cried in the corridor.
Afreen is just as worried about the exams, and says so. But she has kept a plan: lights off by eleven, a twenty-minute walk with her mother after dinner, and proper meals, not biscuits at her desk. This morning she told me, "If I skip sleep, I forget everything I learned anyway."
In today's revision test, Afreen recalled the long answers clearly. Bidisha, usually the stronger student, went blank on two.
What I did next: I spoke to Bidisha privately and gently, suggested she try Afreen's routine for the rest of the week, and I'll check in with her on Friday. I'll also share a short note on rest with all parents.

qa.q: What time does Afreen turn off her lights?
qa.a: Afreen turns her lights off by eleven.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling about the exams?
qa.a: Afreen felt just as worried as others about the exams, but calm enough to trust her routine.

qa.q: What would you advise a student in Bidisha's place?
qa.a: Keep sleep, a short walk and proper meals on schedule, as Afreen does, since tired minds forget what they already know.

qa.q: How was Bidisha affected by studying till three?
qa.a: Bidisha felt exhausted and upset, forgetting a formula she knew and going blank in the test despite being a strong student.

grounding: An adult's note shows a wise student keeping sleep, a walk and meals in exam season, recalling better than one who crams.
